speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have presented with a dermatological condition; please describe the lesions you are concerned about, including their appearance, size, and how long they have been present. To begin our evaluation, have you noticed any changes in their shape, color, or elevation recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for that detailed history; the non-healing, red, crusty lesions on the penis and finger, combined with your significant smoking history and failed prior treatments, are concerning. Given the location and chronic nature of these lesions, have you experienced any pain, itching, bleeding, or rapid growth in these areas?

REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count, CBC_with_Diff, and ESR (Erythrocyte_Sedimentation_Rate) to check for systemic inflammatory markers.
REQUEST IMAGES: Full_Dermoscopy_Penile_Lesion, Full_Dermoscopy_Finger_Lesion.

speaker: Doctor
text: The blood work and inflammatory markers are normal, which helps rule out some systemic inflammatory causes. Have these lesions on your penis and finger caused any bleeding, ulceration, or distinct changes in texture like being hard or scaly? Also, do you have a family history of skin cancer or similar conditions?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Non-healing, crusty, red lesions on the penile shaft and left middle finger. I also have Lesions are painless, History of unsuccessful treatment for syphilis and eczema.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma (Penile and Cutaneous)

The presence of multiple non-healing, painless, crusty lesions in a chronic smoker with a history of failed treatments for syphilis and eczema is highly suggestive of malignancy. The lack of pain does not rule out cancer and may actually support this diagnosis over infectious etiologies that typically present with significant discomfort.
